question: A garden centre started the morning with 34 sacks of compost and sold 16 of them before ten. At midday a lorry delivered 35 more sacks into the yard. Every sack in the yard holds 9 litres of compost. During the afternoon and evening the landscaping team used 86 litres from the yard. The centre prices its compost in cents rather than dollars. How many litres of compost are left?

Early in the morning a cannery stacked 155 crates, and each crate held 4 trays. Every tray carries 2 boxes, and each box contains 8 tins. During the afternoon 8201 tins were shipped out to supermarkets. In the evening a returned order added 19 tins back to the store, and a partner factory sent over 66 more. The cannery employs 74 people on the day shift. How many tins are in the store now?

A stables had 87 bales of hay in the barn and bought 14 more from a neighbour. Every bale can be split into 7 hay nets for the horses. Winter feeding used 174 nets from the pile. A riding school then took 25 nets away for its own ponies. The stables looks after a dozen horses and has 19 stalls in the yard. Feed times are written up in minutes rather than hours. How many nets are left?

Ines had 103 bags of cement stacked at the yard. She used 37 bags on the garage floor. Her partner Bruno, who had far fewer bags of his own, took 30 from her stack for the patio. A merchant then delivered 22 bags to Ines. Another 30 went into the driveway. Every bag still in Ines's stack fills 8 buckets of mix, and the yard bills its deliveries in minutes rather than hours. How many buckets of mix could Ines's remaining cement fill?

Nadia brought 199 apples in from the orchard, and her brother Emil, who picked fewer than she did, added 32 from his own basket. The kitchen used 54 apples for a crumble that afternoon. The rest were shared equally between 3 market boxes, and Nadia took the first box to the stall. She sold 17 apples from that box before the rain started. The orchard has 64 trees. How many apples are left in Nadia's box?

On Monday morning Ramona baked 57 trays of biscuits, and each tray held 5 rows. Every row was made up of 3 biscuits. In the afternoon her partner Ken, who baked fewer trays than Ramona, packed all the biscuits equally into 3 hampers and set the first hamper aside for the school. In the evening 42 biscuits were eaten from that hamper at a tasting. The bakery van holds 26 hampers. How many biscuits are left in the first hamper?

On Saturday morning Tia had 27 tubs of paint in the shed and used 26 of them on the mural. The tub still unopened fills 9 small jars. In the afternoon she shared those jars equally between 3 art tables. In the evening her friend Ola set out 3 tables so that each one matched Tia's first table exactly, jar for jar, though Ola had started the day with far fewer jars than Tia. How many jars did Ola set out on those 3 tables altogether?

In the morning a market gardener cut 26 bunches of daffodils and a helper cut 12 more. Every bunch holds 5 stems. Each stem carries 3 buds. In the afternoon a grower delivered 63 loose buds for the same display. In the evening 236 buds were sold to a hotel. The delivery van had covered 87 kilometres that day. How many buds are left?

A school had 81 packets of seeds and used 77 of them on the vegetable beds. Every packet still in the drawer holds 7 seeds. A parent donated 62 loose seeds to go with them. The seeds were then shared equally between 2 classes, and Class Willow received the first share. The school has a dozen raised beds and a greenhouse 5 metres long. How many seeds did Class Willow receive?

A hospital linen store held 215 pillowcases. An inspection removed 13 that were badly stained. Another 30 went to the day ward, and 88 more were sent up to the new wing. A laundry return then added 75 clean pillowcases to the store. Another 28 went out to the maternity unit. The same team has run this store for a dozen years, and its laundry rota is written in minutes rather than hours. How many pillowcases are in the store now?

A charity shop had 159 books on its shelves in January, and by March its book stock had doubled. A house clearance added 76 more books to the same shelves. Customers then bought 289 books over the spring. A school donated 41 books in April. A car boot sale took another 85 books away from the shop. How many books are on the shelves now?

A club printed 25 sheets of raffle tickets, and each sheet carried 9 tickets. A second printing doubled the number of tickets the club held. A member then brought in 43 tickets left over from last year, and the treasurer found 9 more in a drawer. Before the draw the printer ran off enough extras to double the club's ticket count once again. The club records its meeting lengths in minutes rather than hours. How many tickets does the club have now?

Ahmed loaded 96 crates onto each of 3 lorries. Every crate holds 9 melons. His partner Sara, who loaded fewer crates than Ahmed did, sold 1019 melons at the wholesale market. A supermarket then bought 1543 melons from the same load. The farm covers 55 hectares and has grown melons for a dozen years. How many melons are left?

A joinery had 181 lengths of timber and sent 42 of them back as warped. A merchant delivered 14 more lengths that week, and a cancelled job returned 80 to the rack. Every length on the rack can be cut into 4 shelf boards. Fitting out a library then used 655 of those boards. The workshop is 18 metres long and quotes its jobs in minutes rather than hours. How many shelf boards are left?

Lena had 49 sheets of stamps in her album and bought 28 more at the fair. She swapped 23 sheets away for a poster. The rest she divided equally between 2 folders, keeping the red folder for herself. Her cousin Tobias, who owns fewer stamps than Lena, gave her 70 sheets for the red folder. A dealer sold her another 34 sheets for the same folder. Lena's catalogue prices everything in cents rather than dollars. How many sheets are in the red folder?

Petra had 111 chocolates in a box for the office and found 5 more loose in her bag. Her colleague Denis, who had brought none of his own, handed 79 of them round at the morning meeting. Another 34 went out with the afternoon tea. Petra ate 2 herself before going home. How many chocolates are left in the box?

A stationery shop received 187 boxes of pens, and each box held 4 pens. A supplier added 51 loose pens to the same drawer. A school then bought 276 pens for the new term. A college took another 404 pens for its own students. The shop has traded on this corner for a dozen years. How many pens are left in the drawer?

A depot had 237 crates and sent 28 of them back as damaged. Every crate still in the depot holds 4 boxes. A courier added 40 loose boxes of exactly the same kind. Each box contains 7 tubes of glue. The depot records its shift lengths in minutes rather than hours. How many tubes of glue are in the depot?

A school received 100 boxes of exercise books and sent half of them to the junior building. Of the boxes that stayed, 31 were opened and used at once. Every unopened box still in the store holds 7 books. The office then found 13 loose books in a cupboard and added them to the store. The store has not been tidied since the summer. How many books are in the store now?

A brewery has 237 barrels in the cellar and 57 more standing out in the yard. Every barrel is decanted into 4 kegs. A supplier then delivered 44 ready-filled kegs of the same size. Each keg fills 9 crates of bottles. The brewery's chimney is 22 metres tall. How many crates of bottles can the brewery fill?

On Friday morning Lucia counted 214 boxes of tiles at the depot. Before lunch a delivery added 19 boxes. In the afternoon her colleague Marek, who had ordered fewer boxes than Lucia, brought 32 over from his own store. That evening a returned pallet added 79 more. Every box in the depot holds 3 tiles. The depot's roller door is 5 metres high. How many tiles are in the depot?

A charity split 214 boxes of clothes equally between 2 warehouses. Every box in the first warehouse holds 4 coats. A donor added 38 loose coats to that warehouse. A shelter then collected 172 coats from it. Maria, who runs the first warehouse, had each remaining coat packed with 4 hangers, while her colleague Josef handled far fewer coats at the second site. How many hangers does the first warehouse need?

A nursery filled 72 trays, and each tray held 9 seedlings. A grower delivered 73 loose seedlings, and a school donated 45 more. A landscaping contract then took 703 seedlings away. Frost killed another 34 of the seedlings still on the bench. The nursery has been trading for a dozen years. How many seedlings are left on the bench?

Ronan had 115 sheets of plywood and used 94 of them on the stage set. Every sheet left in the workshop can be cut into 5 panels. His colleague Beata, who had fewer sheets than Ronan to begin with, contributed 71 panels she had already cut. Each panel takes 8 screws to fix in place. A box was dropped and 87 of the screws were lost down a drain. The theatre seats 320 people. How many screws are available for the job?

A club had 134 folding chairs and bought 9 more at auction. A school borrowed 64 of them for a play. A member returned 5 chairs that had been sitting in her garage. The chairs were then shared equally between 3 halls, and the village hall took the first share. Then 3 of that hall's chairs were broken during a ceilidh, and a wedding party took another 24 away. The hall records its bookings in minutes rather than hours. How many chairs are left in the village hall?
